candidate.blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — prevention of complications after diagnostic procedure
candidate.educational_objective: Distinguish prophylaxis from symptom relief after lumbar puncture: routine bed rest is not recommended solely to prevent post-dural-puncture headache.

options.A: Yes. Routine bed rest is recommended after lumbar puncture because it reduces the incidence of post-dural-puncture headache.
options.B: Yes. Because lying flat can relieve headache symptoms, routine bed rest should also be used to prevent the headache from developing.
options.C: Yes. Early mobilization should be avoided because bed rest has a proven prophylactic benefit over mobilization after lumbar puncture.
options.D: No. Routine bed rest is not recommended as prophylaxis; lying flat may provide temporary symptom relief if post-dural-puncture headache later develops.

candidate.rationale: The 2024 multisociety evidence-based guideline on post-dural-puncture headache states that routine bed rest is not recommended as prophylaxis against PDPH. It also notes that lying supine may provide temporary symptom relief when PDPH is already present, but this does not establish prophylactic benefit. Therefore D is correct. A and C incorrectly claim a preventive benefit from routine bed rest, and B incorrectly equates temporary symptom relief with prevention.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Routine bed rest should not be recommended solely to prevent PDPH after dural puncture; supine rest may transiently relieve symptoms once PDPH occurs but does not establish preventive benefit.
candidate.source_document_title: Evidence-based clinical practice guidelines on postdural puncture headache: a consensus report from a multisociety international working group
candidate.source_locator: Prophylactic measures > Bed rest: Recommendation — bed rest is not routinely recommended as prophylaxis against PDPH (Grade D, Moderate Level of Certainty). Conservative measures > Bed rest: temporary symptomatic relief may occur, but routine bed rest is not supported for treatment.
candidate.source_organization: Multisociety International Working Group; published in Regional Anesthesia & Pain Medicine
candidate.source_version_date: Final journal version 2024; current guideline as accessed 2026-08-16
candidate.stem: After an uncomplicated diagnostic lumbar puncture, a client asks whether remaining flat for several hours is necessary solely to prevent a post-dural-puncture headache. Which response is most accurate?
